paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the average cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, as a function of the size of the subset |S|, which ranges from 2 to 10 on a linear scale along the x-axis. The y-axis represents cosine similarity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.1 to 0.5. Two methods are compared: "Weight averaging," represented by a blue dashed line with square markers, and "QAdapter," shown as a green dashed line with circular markers. For "Weight averaging," the cosine similarity starts at approximately 0.48 when |S| = 2 and gradually decreases to about 0.32 at |S| = 10. For "QAdapter," the similarity begins at roughly 0.35 at |S| = 2 and declines to approximately 0.25 at |S| = 10. Both lines exhibit a downward trend, indicating that as the size of the subset S increases, the similarity between the ensemble models and single-task models decreases. The blue line remains consistently above the green line across all values of |S|, reflecting higher similarity for "Weight averaging" compared to "QAdapter" at each subset size.
